resolved_or_reduced: OS NGD Land Theme describes physical and biological land cover while OS NGD Land Use Theme describes human or economic activity
Land polygons and Land Use Site polygons are analytical geography and must not be interpreted as cadastral title or ownership extents
OS NGD Site Access Location is a point where pedestrians or vehicles can enter or exit a site
Access Purpose is populated only for a subset of key public sites and can be NULL for out-of-scope sites
Distance To Network Node is a straight-line measure to the nearest road-network node and is not a routed distance right of way or legal access
OS NGD Field Boundary is a line representing a physical barrier such as hedge wall wooded strip or tree canopy
Field Boundary features can replicate all or part of an underlying Structure Line and are revised through aerial-imagery cycles
A physical Field Boundary line is not proof of legal title boundary ownership or parcel frontage
Ofcom fixed coverage data describes maximum available service capability while fixed performance data relates to active customer connections
Ofcom no longer publishes fixed-performance postcode files from July 2024 because its revised collection is considered robust only down to Local Authority level
Postcode coverage must not be combined with Local Authority performance averages to create synthetic per-postcode or per-UPRN measured speeds
HMLR Title Number and UPRN matching can leave duplicate address records one with title and no UPRN and another with UPRN and no title
A UPRN can exist outside the Land Registry Property Gazetteer and therefore have no linked title while a title can lack a UPRN even when AddressBase contains one
Where one title affects many properties all affecting UPRNs may be associated so title-to-UPRN cardinality is not one-to-one
HMLR refreshes its Land Registry Property Gazetteer using AddressBase change-only updates every six weeks and monthly publication exposes only the latest state
HMLR National Polygon publication validation removes zero-coordinate zero-area and duplicate-coordinate defects and cleans many self-intersections
Polygons with zero area or area below 0.1 square metres are removed from the publication environment
Published National Polygon geometry can therefore differ from production geometry and absence of a sub-0.1 square metre polygon is not evidence of no registered interest
